title: A new method for acquiring images of meiobenthic organisms using the FlowCAM
author: Kitahashi, Watanabe, et al.

steps.title: Collect and preserve sediment cores
steps.instruction: Collect the top 0–1 cm layer from a single sediment core at each station (OT3 65 m, OT4 303 m, OT5 1064 m, OT6 1677 m). Fix the material in 5 % buffered seawater formalin and stain with Rose Bengal to a final concentration of 0.05 g L⁻¹. Store the fixed, stained samples until laboratory processing.

steps.title: Sieve sediment to 63 μm fraction
steps.instruction: In the laboratory, pass each sediment sample sequentially through 1 mm, 250 μm and 63 μm mesh sieves. Retain the material that remains on the 63 μm sieve for further analysis.

steps.title: Resuspend and centrifuge in Ludox
steps.instruction: Resuspend the 63 μm fraction in colloidal silica (Ludox HS‑40, Sigma‑Aldrich; density 1.3 g mL⁻¹). Centrifuge the suspension three times at 800 × g for 10 min each, discarding the supernatant after each spin and re‑suspending the pellet in fresh Ludox before the next spin.

steps.title: Prepare FlowCAM system
steps.instruction: Install the ×4 objective lens on the portable FlowCAM and attach a 300 μm‑thick flow cell. Fill the entire flow line (including inflow tube) with Ludox HS‑40 colloidal silica prior to sample introduction.

steps.title: Introduce sample into FlowCAM
steps.instruction: Gently shake the centrifuged sample to ensure a uniform suspension in Ludox. Pipette the suspension into the FlowCAM flow cell.

steps.title: Capture images of meiobenthos
steps.instruction: Set the FlowCAM to Auto Image mode with an Auto Image Rate of 20 frames s⁻¹. Run the sample and acquire images of all particles passing through the flow cell.

steps.title: Process and classify images
steps.instruction: Process the captured images using VisualSpreadSheet as described in the original method. Assess each image and assign specimens to higher taxonomic levels (e.g., Nematoda, Copepoda).

steps.title: Post‑imaging verification and cleaning
steps.instruction: Re‑collect the sample from the FlowCAM and examine it under a binocular stereoscopic microscope for classification and enumeration. Inspect the original conical tubes, the inflow tube, and the flow cell for any remaining specimens (typically < 3 % remain). After each run, wash the inflow tube and flow cell thoroughly and confirm cleanliness with the stereoscopic microscope.
